definitions.explanation: Running over a long distance at a steady pace to test or build stamina. Commonly used in Japanese school physical education classes as a standard fitness activity.

examples.japanese: {持久走|じきゅうそう}が{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: I'm not good at long-distance running.

examples.japanese: {体育|たいいく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{持久走|じきゅうそう}をした。
examples.english: We did an endurance run in PE class.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}になると{学校|がっこう}で{持久走|じきゅうそう}{大会|たいかい}がある。
examples.english: In winter, schools hold endurance-running competitions.

examples.japanese: {持久走|じきゅうそう}を{続|つづ}けていると、{体力|たいりょく}がついてくる。
examples.english: If you keep doing endurance running, you build up stamina.

notes:
Composed of {持久|じきゅう} (endurance, lasting) + {走|そう} (running). Refers specifically to long-distance running as a form of exercise or fitness testing. In Japanese schools, {持久走|じきゅうそう} is a staple of winter PE classes, often culminating in a {持久走|じきゅうそう}{大会|たいかい} (endurance-running competition) where students run distances from 1 km up to several kilometers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}{大会|たいかい}: endurance-run competition
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}が{苦手|にがて}: bad at endurance running
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}をする: to do endurance running
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}の{練習|れんしゅう}: endurance-running practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マラソン: marathon — technically a specific 42.195 km race, but used loosely in Japanese for any long-distance run
- {長距離走|ちょうきょりそう}: long-distance running — the formal athletic-event term
- ジョギング: jogging — more casual, for fitness at a relaxed pace

CULTURAL NOTE:
{持久走|じきゅうそう}{大会|たいかい} is a well-known Japanese school event, often associated with cold winter weather and mixed feelings among students — seen as tough training but also a rite of passage.
